title: The farmer who dug up the oldest zero in the world
hook: The oldest known zero was dug up by a farmer.
summary: A farmer found the Bakhshali manuscript in 1881, and in 2017 radiocarbon dating showed its dot zero is centuries older than any zero known before.
sources: Bodleian Libraries, University of Oxford (2017): radiocarbon dating of the Bakhshali manuscript, oldest pages dated to about 224-383 CE.
Encyclopaedia Britannica / Wikipedia: Bakhshali manuscript, found 1881 by a farmer in Bakhshali, near Peshawar (now Pakistan), birch bark, dot used as placeholder.

lines.text: The oldest known zero was dug up by a farmer.
lines.caps: The oldest *zero | was *dug up | by a *farmer

lines.text: In eighteen eighty-one, in Bakhshali, now Pakistan, he found pages of birch bark.
They used a small dot as a placeholder, the seed of our zero.
lines.caps: A small *dot | as a *placeholder, | the seed of *zero

lines.text: Scholars argued about its age for over a hundred years.
Then in twenty seventeen, Oxford scientists tested it with radiocarbon dating.
The oldest pages were about seventeen hundred years old.
That is centuries older than any zero known before.
A dot from a field changed maths.

post.caption:
A tiny dot in a farmer's field changed the story of maths.
